As one of the nation’s foremost scientifc institutions, Photo by Dennis Schroeder, NREL 27807 the laboratory embraces the best in energy operational practices and ecological management, setting the standard for the wise use of natural resources. NREL’s goal is to minimize the use of energy, materials, and water while meeting all research needs. In all site development, opportunities to integrate energy efciency and innovative on-site energy, and high-performance buildings are sought. NREL’s dedication to resource optimization supports the laboratory’s success by applying what is learned, through R&D, to campus facilities and infrastructure systems. 3.1 Resource Optimization Goals NREL updates an Energy and Water Management Dashboard and Narrative every year to report on past performance and set goals for the coming year. These performance goals are integrated into the laboratory’s EMS. To meet DOE energy and water performance goals, efciency considerations are incorporated into operations. The goals address: • Energy, water, and waste management. • Building design, construction, and ongoing maintenance. • Environmental management planning. • Strategic purchasing. • Resilience planning. • Measurement and tracking of environmental objectives, targets, and actions. • Awareness and engagement of staf and community members.
